record.paper_title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS
record.original_question: Let f_d be any seed whose associated operators are Schur-positive, and write f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(f_d)(1). Let the linear operator overline{·} on Schur functions be defined by overline{s_μ} = s_{ ar μ}, where  ar μ is obtained by removing the first column of μ, and extend this operator linearly so expressions of different total degree can be compared. For coprime integers b ≥ a ≥ 1, is it always true that f^{(b,a)}_d(x;q,t) ⪯_s f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) after this comparison, for every seed f_d that gives rise to Schur-positive expressions?

evidence.quote: For a partition µ, let us denote by µ̄ the partition obtained by removing the first column of µ. Then, we set sµ(x) := sµ̄(x), and extend linearly to all symmetric functions.
Question.5. Can we prove that f(b,a)d (x; q, t) ⪯s f(a,b)d (x; q, t), for all coprime b ≥ a ≥ 1, and any seed fd that gives rise to Schur positive expressions?

We underline that the functions f(b,a)d (x; q, t) and f(a,b)d (x; q, t) are of different degrees; equal to ad in the first case, and bd in the second. Hence they can only be compared after applying the (−) operator, which results in a symmetric function having components of various degrees.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring of symmetric functions in variables $x = (x_1, x_2, \ldots)$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$. For each pair of coprime positive integers $(a,b)$ with $b \geq a \geq 1$, let $\Theta_{a,b}$ denote the family of operators on symmetric functions associated with rectangular $(a,b)$-Catalan combinatorics (the "nabla-like" operators indexed by coprime slopes acting on a chosen seed). For a degree-$d$ seed $f_d$ such that the symmetric function 
$$ f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) \;:=\; \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(1) $$
is Schur-positive (i.e., its expansion in the Schur basis $\{s_\lambda\}$ has coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$), the function $f^{(a,b)}_d$ is homogeneous of degree $bd$, and $f^{(b,a)}_d$ is homogeneous of degree $ad$.

Define a linear operator $\overline{(\cdot)}$ on symmetric functions by setting, for every partition $\mu$,
$$ \overline{s_\mu} \;:=\; s_{\bar\mu}, $$
where $\bar\mu$ is the partition obtained by removing the first column of $\mu$ (equivalently, subtracting $1$ from each nonzero part), and extending linearly to all symmetric functions. The image $\overline{f}$ of a homogeneous symmetric function may have components of several degrees, allowing comparison of expressions of different total degree.

Given two symmetric functions $F, G$, write $F \preceq_s G$ if $G - F$ is Schur-positive, where the comparison is applied after $\overline{(\cdot)}$, i.e., $\overline{F} \preceq_s \overline{G}$ in the Schur basis.

Question: Is it true that for every pair of coprime integers $b \geq a \geq 1$ and every seed $f_d$ for which both $f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t)$ and $f^{(b,a)}_d(x;q,t)$ are Schur-positive, one has
$$ \overline{f^{(b,a)}_d(x;q,t)} \;\preceq_s\; \overline{f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t)}\, ? $$

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or refutation of this Schur-positivity comparison between $\Theta_{a,b}$ and $\Theta_{b,a}$ images across coprime slopes after column-removal. Related work on rational $(a,b)$-Catalan and $k$-Schur positivity exists, but no source directly resolves this specific transpose sub-symmetry question; status remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Open Questions for operators related to Rectangular Catalan Combinatorics
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates open questions on Schur positivity for operators in rectangular Catalan combinatorics.
status_evidence.claim: Original venue listing the question; no resolution indicated.

status_evidence.title: Catalan Functions and k-Schur Positivity
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Schur and k-Schur positivity of Catalan functions, related but does not address this transpose comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Related Schur-positivity literature does not contain a proof of the precise statement.

status_evidence.title: Rational Parking Functions and Catalan Numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Treats rational (a,b) coprime parking functions and Frobenius characters.
status_evidence.claim: Background on coprime (a,b) constructions; no proof of the comparison conjecture.
